- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.11 to +0.17 in recent days).  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or shows strong bearish signals (e.g., -0.28 to -0.33).  
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecasts by applying a 3-5 day moving average if sentiment volatility exceeds 0.20.  
- Avoid sharp downward corrections after high forecasts; if forecast drops >5% from peak, reduce subsequent forecast by 10-15% to prevent overshoot.  
- Mean-reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, adjust downward by 2-4% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the period (first 5-7 days) when sentiment is volatile; reduce first 5 days by 1-2% if sentiment is mixed or negative.
